headline.purpose: Page titles and major empty or error states.

title.purpose: Card titles, device names, and section headings.

body.purpose: Descriptions, table content, and operational copy.

label.purpose: Metric labels, navigation group labels, and compact metadata headings.

technical.purpose: IP addresses, MAC addresses, ports, timestamps, and machine-oriented values.

shadows.name: overlay-separation
shadows.purpose: Separates dialogs and high-priority floating surfaces from the dashboard.

shadows.name: tooltip-separation
shadows.purpose: Separates explanatory hover and focus content without lifting resting cards.

motion.name: standard-transition
motion.purpose: Brief color, opacity, and focus-state transitions.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes non-essential animation and shortens transitions for users who request reduced motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Decisive actions such as starting a scan or saving a policy.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); border: 0; border-radius: 9px; padding: 8px 16px; height: 36px; font: 500 0.875rem/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Low-emphasis navigation and utility actions that should not compete with a scan.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--muted-foreground); border: 0; border-radius: 9px; padding: 8px 12px; height: 36px; font: 500 0.875rem/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--accent); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Technical Input
components.description: Compact field for subnet, domain, search, and configuration values.
components.css: .ds-input { background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: 9px; padding: 4px 12px; height: 36px; width: 100%; font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; border-color: var(--ring); }

components.name: Panel Card
components.description: Flat resting container for one operational topic, metric group, or workflow step.
components.html:
Network readiness

Sensor connected and collecting evidence.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--card); color: var(--card-foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; padding: 20px; } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0; font: 600 1rem/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-card p { margin: 6px 0 0; color: var(--muted-foreground); font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Compact status or severity label that pairs semantic color with readable text.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; width: fit-content; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 10px; font: 600 0.6875rem/1.4 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; } .ds-chip-success { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, #34d399 25%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklab, #34d399 10%, transparent); color: #34d399; } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation Item
components.description: Compact rail item that keeps location visible while preserving room for evidence.
components.html: Devices
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--muted-foreground); text-decoration: none; font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-nav-item svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 60%, transparent); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-nav-item-active { background: var(--accent); color: var(--foreground); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
NetWatch presents network state as a focused control surface for quick detection and response. The radar metaphor is about signal quality, not science-fiction decoration: the interface should tell the administrator what changed, where it happened, and what action is actually possible.

The incumbent system uses a dark neutral field with a cool blue signal accent, restrained tonal layering, and compact operational modules. Typography stays quiet and technical: Geist supports reading and decisions, while Geist Mono identifies IP addresses, MAC addresses, ports, timestamps, and other evidence. The voice is direct and incident-oriented, preferring evidence and next action over spectacle.

The visual system deliberately avoids hacker theatre, Matrix-style backgrounds, neon green dominance, decorative gradients, excessive glow, fake terminal text, and animation that competes with network state.
keyCharacteristics: Radar-like prioritization of live network signals.
Cool blue action accent used with intention.
Flat resting surfaces with restrained tonal layers.
Direct copy that leads with evidence and consequence.
Technical identifiers set in a selective monospace voice.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Reserve the primary blue accent for actions, active state, focus, and meaningful network signal; the interface should remain calm when nothing needs attention.

rules.name: The Evidence Before Drama Rule
rules.body: Let type hierarchy expose what changed and what can be done; do not enlarge or decorate a value merely to make the screen feel more active.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Resting cards and panels use border and tonal contrast; elevation appears only when a surface is actually layered above another surface.

dos: Do reserve the primary blue accent for meaningful actions, active navigation, focus, and live network signal.
Do use Geist Mono selectively for IP addresses, MAC addresses, ports, timestamps, and other technical identifiers.
Do pair every status color with text or a shape cue so state remains understandable without color perception.
Do keep resting surfaces flat and let borders and tonal layers establish structure.
Do lead incident copy with the observed evidence, affected device, time, and available next action.
Do preserve generous content grouping while keeping individual rows compact enough to scan.
donts: Don't use Matrix backgrounds, fake terminal text, neon green dominance, decorative gradients, or gratuitous glow.
Don't make every card or navigation item blue; signal loses meaning when everything is highlighted.
Don't use shadows on ordinary resting cards when a border and tonal layer already provide separation.
Don't communicate severity or device state through color alone.
Don't invent activity, device identity, topology, or certainty in order to make an empty state look busy.
Don't expose raw backend errors or turn technical limitations into unexplained dead ends.
